target.title: refactor(infra): establish shared error normalization foundation
target.body:
this is exploratory, may or may not iterate on this
Related: #99314 

## What Problem This Solves

Generic unknown-error handling is duplicated across core and bundled plugins, with inconsistent behavior for causes, numeric codes, circular values, native platform errors, accessors, and serialization. This makes later caller migrations risky because there is not yet one fully specified core contract to migrate toward.

## Why This Change Was Made

This establishes the first of four bounded consolidation PRs. It hardens `src/infra/errors.ts` as the canonical core owner, adds a cycle-safe `serializeError` projection, preserves native and inherited `Error` diagnostics, and avoids executing hostile own accessors during normalization. Caller migrations and plugin SDK exposure remain intentionally out of scope for this foundation PR.

## User Impact

No intended user-visible behavior change. Maintainers gain a tested canonical error contract that later PRs can use to remove duplicated coercion and formatting helpers safely.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/errors.test.ts` — 34 tests passed.
- `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs src/infra/errors.ts src/infra/errors.test.ts` — passed.
- `pnpm exec oxfmt --check src/infra/errors.ts src/infra/errors.test.ts` — passed.
- `OPENCLAW_HEAVY_CHECK_LOCK_SCOPE=worktree pnpm tsgo:core` — passed.
- `OPENCLAW_HEAVY_CHECK_LOCK_SCOPE=worktree pnpm tsgo:core:test` — passed.
- `.agents/skills/autoreview/scripts/autoreview --mode local --engine codex --stream-engine-output` — clean after addressing accessor safety, DOMException compatibility, inherited Error diagnostics, hostile cause serialization, and lazy fallback reads.
- Production diff: +179 lines for the shared foundation. The complete four-PR series is estimated to remove approximately 500–700 net production lines; 38 exact coercion copies currently account for 496 lines by themselves.
